etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Middle French sceptique (but with a pronunciation closer to that of the Latin etymon), or possibly directly from Late Latin scepticus (originally attested only in the plural Scepticī (“the sect of Skeptics”)), from Proto-Italic *spektos (“see, observing”), from *speḱ- (“to see”), compare to σκοπέω (skopéō, “to view, examine”).
This word was originally spelled sceptick or sceptic and pronounced like septic, the /k/ is a result of learned influence.
senses: Someone who doubts beliefs, claims, plans, etc. that are accepted by others as true or appropriate, especially one who habitually does so.
(in particular) Someone who is skeptical towards religion.
